summary: Woman ~3 weeks status post exam under anesthesia, extensive lysis of adhesions, total laparoscopic hysterectomy with bilateral salpingectomy and cystoscopy, presenting with acute heavy vaginal bleeding with clots after an initial period of only light spotting. Clinic exam showed no cuff dehiscence and a small bleeding vessel was cauterized; pelvic ultrasound showed a normal vaginal cuff with no hematoma. Hematocrit 38.1 (preop 40.1), hemodynamically stable, no procedure required this stay; bleeding decreased with observation and she was discharged on hospital day 2.
most_likely: Postprocedural hemorrhage from vaginal cuff following total laparoscopic hysterectomy

differential.diagnosis: Postprocedural hemorrhage from vaginal cuff following total laparoscopic hysterectomy
supporting_evidence: Chief complaint: heavy vaginal bleeding after hysterectomy
Small vessel at cuff cauterized in clinic
TLH/BS with extensive lysis of adhesions ~3 weeks prior
opposing_evidence: No transfusion or operative intervention required
differential.reasoning: Bleeding is directly attributable to the recent hysterectomy site with an identified cuff vessel cauterized; this is the principal disease driving the admission for observation.

differential.diagnosis: Vaginal cuff granulation tissue with bleeding vessel
supporting_evidence: Small vessel cauterized at cuff in clinic
Ultrasound: normal-appearing vaginal cuff, normal postoperative changes
opposing_evidence: Granulation tissue not explicitly described in note
differential.reasoning: Delayed cuff bleeding at 3 weeks postop commonly arises from healing granulation tissue/suture-line vessel; supported indirectly by successful cautery.

supporting_evidence: PMH hypothyroidism; Synthroid 50 mcg continued inpatient
opposing_evidence: No thyroid labs recorded this stay
differential.reasoning: Chronic comorbidity actively managed during the stay, appropriate as a secondary coded condition.

differential.diagnosis: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder on stimulant therapy
differential.reasoning: Documented chronic condition with continued medication during admission.

differential.diagnosis: Depressive disorder / anxiety on venlafaxine therapy
supporting_evidence: Prior billing included F329 and F419
opposing_evidence: Current note attributes venlafaxine to ADHD history, no mood symptoms documented
differential.reasoning: Supported mainly by prior coding and ongoing SNRI therapy; current documentation is ambiguous.

supporting_evidence: Heavy vaginal bleeding with clots in early postoperative period
opposing_evidence: Clinic exam: no evidence of cuff dehiscence
differential.reasoning: Important and dangerous differential for postop cuff bleeding but explicitly excluded on direct examination and imaging.

differential.diagnosis: Acute blood loss anemia from vaginal hemorrhage
supporting_evidence: Reported heavy bleeding with passage of large clots
opposing_evidence: Patient denies symptoms of acute blood loss anemia
differential.reasoning: Explicitly considered but not met — hematocrit essentially stable and patient asymptomatic, so unlikely to be codable.

supporting_evidence: Ultrasound indication was to evaluate for cuff hematoma
opposing_evidence: Ultrasound impression: no vaginal cuff hematoma, no free fluid
differential.reasoning: Considered clinically and imaged, but definitively excluded by transabdominal/transvaginal pelvic ultrasound.

rule_outs.why: No dehiscence on clinic exam; ultrasound shows intact, normal-appearing cuff
Pelvic ultrasound explicitly shows no hematoma and no free fluid

rule_outs.diagnosis: Hemorrhagic shock / significant blood loss requiring transfusion
rule_outs.why: Hemodynamically stable throughout, Hct 38.1 near baseline, no transfusion given

rule_outs.diagnosis: Retained products or recurrent uterine bleeding
rule_outs.why: Uterus surgically absent on imaging; bleeding is cuff-derived
No fever, WBC 8.7 normal, no purulent discharge documented

uncertain_areas: Whether documentation specifies granulation tissue versus simple postprocedural hemorrhage at cuff
Whether the clinic cautery was coded as a procedure during this admission
Timing/attribution of bleeding as postprocedural complication versus routine postoperative bleeding
Coder treatment of thrombocytosis (PLT 434) and microcytosis (MCV 80) with normal hemoglobin
Whether depression/anxiety were actively addressed this stay or are historical only
